details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/task_state.py:189-194 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: A dependent task file could be a symlink and the code will write through it.
  WHY: The symlink check only covers the completed issue’s own file, so rewriting dependent `.tasks/<wave>/*.json` files can escape the task-state directory; all reviewers rated this at least major/high.
- scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:lines 2204-2218 (_maybe_unblock_task_state_dependents) | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: Runtime `inspect.signature()` probing is used on every issue completion to decide whether to pass `completed_issue_payload`.
  WHY: Reviewers agreed it is brittle and adds hot-path overhead, with severity reported from nit to major, so the highest severity is used.
- scripts/task_state.py:lines 140-150 (_candidate_blocker_tokens) and lines 206-210 (unblock_dependents) | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: When `completed_issue_payload` is supplied, only `github_issue` is extracted and the rest of the payload is ignored.
  WHY: Callers expecting the supplied payload to be authoritative can get incomplete data instead of the full `read_task()` payload; reviewers split between nit and major, so high is used.
- scripts/render_prompt.py / scripts/render_prompt.sh:render_prompt.py lost ~250 lines, render_prompt.sh gained ~285 lines | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The identity-reinject implementation was removed from Python and reimplemented in shell, changing the code path.
  WHY: The shell migration changes error handling and temp-file/trap behavior, and some reviewers explicitly treated it as an intentional migration rather than a bug, so this is disputed.
- scripts/render_prompt.sh:line 261, `trap cleanup_temp_files EXIT` inside `inject_identity_recall_block`; line 491, `trap cleanup_temp_files EXIT` | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: `trap cleanup_temp_files EXIT` replaces any prior EXIT handler instead of chaining it.
  WHY: A later or earlier EXIT hook can be silently dropped, which can orphan cleanup steps; reviewers described it as structurally fragile but currently harmless.
- scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:2211 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: Adding `completed_issue_payload=issue` changes the public helper signature for `unblock_dependents`.
  WHY: Direct callers using the old two-argument form can break unless the compatibility shim always succeeds.
- tests/test_task_state_unblock.py:test_unblock_dependents_uses_supplied_completed_issue_payload_for_github_issue_tokens | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The new test only exercises the happy path and misses invalid/missing payload cases.
  WHY: That can hide regressions that reintroduce `read_task()` or mishandle non-dict payloads.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/render_prompt.sh:line 261, `trap cleanup_temp_files EXIT` inside `inject_identity_recall_block` | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The trap command inside `inject_identity_recall_block` unconditionally overwrites any prior EXIT trap registered earlier in the script rather than chaining it.
  WHY: A future addition of a second EXIT trap elsewhere in the script would silently lose its handler, potentially orphaning temp files or skipping cleanup hooks.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- scripts/task_state.py:lines 189-194 (unblock_dependents function) | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The symlink check only applies to the completed issue's own file (wave_dir), but not the dependent task files being rewritten in the loop.
  WHY: A dependent task file could be a symlink pointing outside `.tasks/`, and the code will write through it, risking corruption outside `.tasks/`.
- scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:lines 2207-2215 (_maybe_unblock_task_state_dependents) | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Using `inspect.signature()` at runtime on every issue completion to probe whether the new parameter exists is both slow and brittle. (2 related items)
  WHY: If the function signature changes in the future or a decorator is added, detection can silently fail and fall back to the old path; repeated introspection also adds latency in the hot path.
- scripts/task_state.py:lines 140-150 (_candidate_blocker_tokens) | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: When `completed_issue_payload` is supplied, it's used only for extracting the `github_issue` token and the full payload is not propagated for any other use case.
  WHY: Callers that expect the payload to be authoritative for all fields will get incomplete data.
- scripts/render_prompt.sh / scripts/render_prompt.py:render_prompt.py lost ~250 lines, render_prompt.sh gained ~285 lines | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The identity-reinject functionality was moved from Python to shell, and the Python implementation is completely removed.
  WHY: If any code path still relies on the Python implementation, it will silently fail or produce different results because the shell implementation has different error-handling, trap cleanup, and parsing behavior.
- scripts/render_prompt.sh:line 261 and line 491, `trap cleanup_temp_files EXIT` | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Setting `trap cleanup_temp_files EXIT` inside functions replaces any existing EXIT handler wholesale rather than chaining it.
  WHY: If inject_identity_recall_block is called after another trap is set, it will silently drop the previous cleanup.

  Expected change site: `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` (the write checkpoints) and the corresponding wiring in `orchestrate_lib.py` for wave completion
  Evidence of absence: No diff hunk in `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` (PR changed files list does not even include it). The only call site updated is inside `scripts/orchestrate_lib.py::_maybe_unblock_task_state_dependents`.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER

- requirement: "Add `.tasks/` to `.gitignore`."
  Expected change site: `.gitignore`
  Evidence of absence: No change to `.gitignore`; the new directory will be committed on every run.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- requirement: "Document the schema in `agents.md` under a new 'Task-state files' sub-section"
  Expected change site: `agents.md` (near the existing task-state section)
  Evidence of absence: No update to agents.md in the PR diff. The new test and code are undocumented.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR

  WHY: If the function signature changes or if signature inspection is restricted in certain Python configurations, the branch could silently fall back to the no-payload path or re-read the task file from disk.
